summary: Custom Markdown references now inherit the package runtime color policy only when the policy namespace is completely absent; malformed checksum markers and partial policy blocks fail closed.
decisions: Detect runtime-policy presence with exact namespace sentinels for the begin prefix, end marker, and typed JSON fence instead of the strict checksum regex alone.
Require exactly one begin marker, end marker, and typed fence whenever any policy namespace sentinel is present.
Reject non-hex and short SHA-256 tokens before any package-default inheritance can occur.
Treat orphaned end markers and typed fences as partial policy corruption, not as policy absence.
Preserve package-default inheritance for custom references that contain no runtime-policy namespace sentinel at all.

gate_results.evidence: 21 passed, including non-hex checksum, short checksum, marker-free inheritance, normal custom policy, orphaned end marker, and orphaned typed fence cases.

gate_results.command: uv run pytest <semantic color, adapter, token, style, and graph targets> -q
uv run ruff check design_ontology_harness/semantic_color_markdown.py tests/test_semantic_color_markdown.py && git diff --check
gate_results.evidence: All checks passed with no whitespace errors.
ok=true, changed=false, payload SHA and runtime policy SHA unchanged, Pantone COY identity count=29.

risks: The sentinel check is intentionally strict: literal policy marker or fence syntax in unrelated custom prose is treated as a malformed policy block rather than ignored.
